task: Make the llmc proxy model lock survive proxy restarts by persisting it through the state file. Today ctx.lock_model / ctx.lock_owners are in-memory only; a proxy restart silently clears the lock (observed live: the lock cleared on every make restart). The state layer is ALREADY plumbed: llmc/state.py's State dataclass has lock_owners (list[str]) with TOML round-trip and load() validation. THE CHANGE, four small pieces: (1) state.py: add an optional `locked: Optional[str] = None` field to State - to_toml() writes `locked = "<preset>"` only when set, load() parses/validates it (string or omitted) and adds "locked" to its allowed-keys set. (2) proxy.py restore path: when a ProxyContext is built, derive the lock from the loaded state - lock_model = state.locked, lock_owners = set(state.lock_owners). Cleanest is a ProxyContext.__post_init__ so EVERY construction (build_context, tests, probes) restores consistently. (3) proxy.py persist path: in _handle_mode_post's lock block, after every mutation (set, owner-release, force-clear), write through with ctx.state = state_mod.update(ctx.config.state_path, locked=<current lock_model or omit-when-None>, lock_owners=<sorted list>) - note state_mod.update uses dataclasses.replace, so pass locked=None explicitly to clear it. CRITICAL: the write must be wrapped so an OSError (unwritable state dir) logs a warning and the lock still works in-memory - the existing TestModelLock tests use the DEFAULT state_dir (/state, unwritable in dev) and must keep passing UNMODIFIED; a 500 on lock set is a failure. (4) ADD unit tests: state round-trip for locked+lock_owners (test_state.py), and a restart-restore test in test_proxy.py (lock over HTTP with a tmp state_dir, rebuild the context from the same state_dir, assert the lock is back). ADD ONLY - do not modify existing tests. THE CONTRACT IS PINNED by .pi/lock-persistence-probe.py (operator-owned, do NOT modify): it boots your proxy with a temp state dir, locks with two owners, simulates restarts by rebuilding the context from the same state file, and asserts the lock + owners + enforcement survive; also that an unwritable state dir degrades gracefully. python3 .pi/lock-persistence-probe.py must go green, and .pi/lock-owners-probe.py must STAY green.
rules: Only files under llmc/ may change. Nothing under .pi/ - the probes are operator-owned.

EDIT DISCIPLINE (this is where previous attempts failed): never rewrite a whole file. Use the edit tool with oldText copied character-for-character from a fresh read of the exact lines you are changing - 4-space indentation, reproduced exactly. Small hunks only.

After EVERY edit, before doing anything else, run: python3 -c 'import llmc.proxy, llmc.state' - a syntax/indentation error means your last edit was malformed; fix THAT line immediately instead of pressing on.
Existing tests must pass unmodified - especially TestModelLock, which uses the default unwritable /state dir: your persistence write MUST tolerate OSError there (log + continue in-memory), never 500.
Do not rebuild, restart, or docker-touch any container; this is a code-only change.
A check satisfied by editing tests, the probes, or special-casing probe requests is a FAILED iteration.

sensors.cmd: judge --base HEAD --model openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3 --spec 'Restart-safe model lock for the llmc proxy. Acceptance criteria: (1) State gains an optional locked field with TOML round-trip and load() validation (allowed-keys updated); (2) ProxyContext derives lock_model/lock_owners from the loaded state on construction so a proxy restart restores the lock; (3) every lock mutation in _handle_mode_post persists via state_mod.update, tolerating OSError (unwritable state dir) with a log line while the lock keeps working in-memory - the pre-existing TestModelLock tests use the default unwritable /state and must pass UNMODIFIED; (4) new add-only unit tests cover the state round-trip and restart restore; (5) enforcement semantics are unchanged; (6) changes confined to llmc/; (7) ignore .pi/** - operator scaffolding. Reject: weakened or modified existing tests, whole-file rewrites, persistence failures that 500 the lock API, scope creep, justifying essays in comments.'
